questions.question_text: Which ethical principle recognises a patient's right to make informed decisions about their own healthcare?

choices.text: Beneficence
Autonomy
Justice
Fidelity

questions.rationale: Autonomy is the ethical principle that respects an individual's right to make voluntary and informed decisions about personal healthcare. Nurses should provide appropriate information and respect a patient's competent choices.

questions.question_text: Which ethical principle requires a nurse to act in ways that promote the well-being of patients?

choices.text: Beneficence
Veracity
Autonomy
Confidentiality

questions.rationale: Beneficence refers to the duty to do good and promote the welfare of patients. It guides nurses to provide care that benefits patients and supports positive health outcomes.

questions.question_text: The ethical principle of non-maleficence is best described as:

choices.text: Treating every patient according to social status
Avoiding actions that may cause unnecessary harm
Keeping every promise made to colleagues
Providing patients with all available information

questions.rationale: Non-maleficence means avoiding harm or preventing unnecessary injury to patients. Nurses apply this principle by practising safely, recognising risks and avoiding interventions that may cause preventable harm.

questions.question_text: Which ethical principle requires fair and equitable treatment of patients regardless of their background?

choices.text: Fidelity
Veracity
Justice
Autonomy

questions.rationale: Justice concerns fairness and equitable distribution of healthcare resources and services. Nurses should not discriminate against patients because of their ethnicity, religion, gender, disability or socioeconomic status.

questions.question_text: A nurse honestly explains a patient's diagnosis and treatment options without deliberately misleading the patient. Which ethical principle is demonstrated?

choices.text: Veracity
Fidelity
Justice
Non-maleficence

questions.rationale: Veracity is the ethical obligation to tell the truth and provide accurate information. It supports trust and enables patients to make informed decisions about their healthcare.

questions.question_text: Which ethical principle involves keeping professional promises and fulfilling commitments made to patients?

choices.text: Autonomy
Beneficence
Fidelity
Justice

questions.rationale: Fidelity refers to faithfulness, trustworthiness and keeping professional commitments. Nurses demonstrate fidelity by carrying out agreed responsibilities and maintaining trustworthy relationships with patients.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of the Nursing and Midwifery Council's Code of Professional Conduct?

choices.text: To establish standards of professional behaviour and practice
To determine the financial charges of every health facility
To replace all clinical guidelines used in hospitals
To regulate the employment conditions of every public servant

questions.rationale: The N&MC Code of Professional Conduct provides standards that guide nurses' professional behaviour, ethical responsibilities and relationships with patients and colleagues. It supports public protection and professional accountability.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a fundamental right recognised in the Patients' Charter in Ghana?

choices.text: The right to demand any treatment regardless of clinical indication
The right to receive information about one's health condition and proposed care
The right to access another patient's medical records
The right to refuse all facility rules without consequences

questions.rationale: The Patients' Charter recognises patients' rights to information about their health and the care being provided. Such information supports participation in healthcare decisions and informed consent.

questions.question_text: Which statement best defines informed consent in nursing practice?

choices.text: Permission obtained from a patient without explaining the proposed procedure
Voluntary agreement given after receiving relevant information and understanding the proposed intervention
Permission automatically assumed whenever a patient enters a hospital
Approval given by a nurse on behalf of every adult patient

questions.rationale: Informed consent requires adequate information, understanding, voluntariness and decision-making capacity. A patient's agreement should not be obtained through coercion, deception or improper pressure.

questions.question_text: What is the meaning of confidentiality in nursing practice?

choices.text: Keeping all health information secret even from professionals involved in necessary care
Protecting patient information from unauthorised access, use or disclosure
Allowing family members unrestricted access to patient records
Avoiding documentation of sensitive health conditions

questions.rationale: Confidentiality is the professional duty to protect information obtained through the nurse-patient relationship. Information may be shared when properly authorised or when disclosure is legally justified or required.

questions.question_text: In nursing practice, negligence is best described as:

choices.text: A deliberate refusal to follow a patient's personal preference
Failure to exercise the reasonable standard of care expected, resulting in harm
Any disagreement between a nurse and a patient
A patient's refusal to follow health education advice

questions.rationale: Negligence involves a breach of a duty of care through failure to meet the required standard, causing harm or damage. Whether negligence has occurred depends on the relevant facts and applicable legal principles.

questions.question_text: Why can nursing documentation be important in legal proceedings?

choices.text: It provides a contemporaneous record of assessments, decisions and care provided
It automatically proves that every nursing action was correct
It removes the need for nurses to explain their professional decisions
It prevents patients from making complaints

questions.rationale: Patient records may provide evidence of the care delivered, observations made and decisions taken. Accurate and timely documentation supports accountability, continuity of care and legal review.

questions.question_text: What is patient advocacy in nursing?

choices.text: Making every healthcare decision without consulting the patient
Supporting and protecting patients' rights, interests and informed choices
Persuading patients to accept every proposed intervention
Prioritising the convenience of healthcare workers over patient welfare

questions.rationale: Patient advocacy involves promoting patients' rights, safety, dignity and access to appropriate information and care. Nurses help patients express their concerns and participate in decisions affecting their health.

questions.question_text: What are professional boundaries in nursing?

choices.text: Limits that maintain a safe and appropriate professional relationship with patients
Rules preventing nurses from communicating with patients
Personal preferences that allow nurses to choose which patients to treat
Restrictions that apply only when nurses work in hospitals

questions.rationale: Professional boundaries define appropriate limits within the nurse-patient relationship. They protect patients from exploitation and help maintain trust, objectivity and professional integrity.

questions.question_text: In nursing practice, whistleblowing refers to:

choices.text: Reporting suspected wrongdoing or unsafe practice through appropriate channels
Discussing colleagues' personal lives with patients
Refusing to participate in any professional meeting
Publishing confidential patient information to attract public attention

questions.rationale: Whistleblowing involves raising concerns about suspected misconduct, unsafe practice or wrongdoing through appropriate reporting mechanisms. It supports patient safety, professional accountability and organisational integrity.

questions.question_text: A competent adult patient refuses a recommended treatment after receiving an adequate explanation. Which ethical principle most directly supports respecting this decision?

choices.text: Autonomy
Beneficence
Fidelity
Justice

questions.rationale: Autonomy protects the right of a competent patient to make informed decisions, including refusing recommended treatment. The nurse should explore the patient's concerns, explain possible consequences and document the discussion appropriately.

questions.question_text: A nurse notices that a patient is at risk of falling and places the patient in a safer position while arranging assistance. Which ethical principle is primarily demonstrated?

choices.text: Veracity
Non-maleficence
Fidelity
Autonomy

questions.rationale: Non-maleficence requires nurses to take reasonable steps to prevent avoidable harm. Reducing a patient's risk of falling is an example of applying this principle in routine care.

questions.question_text: Two patients require the same limited emergency resource. The nurse allocates it according to clinical urgency rather than wealth or social position. Which ethical principle guides this decision?

choices.text: Justice
Fidelity
Veracity
Autonomy

questions.rationale: Justice requires fair allocation of healthcare resources based on relevant and ethically defensible criteria. Clinical urgency is an appropriate consideration, whereas wealth and social status should not determine access to care.

questions.question_text: A nurse is asked to perform a clinical procedure for which the nurse has not received appropriate training. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Perform the procedure to avoid criticism from colleagues
Explain the limitation and seek assistance from a suitably competent practitioner
Ask a patient to guide the procedure
Perform the procedure without supervision and avoid documenting it

questions.rationale: Nurses are expected to practise within their competence and professional scope. Seeking appropriate assistance protects patients and demonstrates professional accountability.

questions.question_text: A nurse working at a CHPS compound notices that a colleague repeatedly arrives for duty while apparently impaired by alcohol. What is the most appropriate professional response?

choices.text: Ignore the behaviour because the colleague is experienced
Take immediate steps to protect patients and report the concern through the appropriate supervisory channels
Allow the colleague to continue performing procedures without supervision
Discuss the matter publicly with community members

questions.rationale: A practitioner whose fitness to practise may be impaired can place patients at risk. The nurse should prioritise patient safety and report the concern through appropriate professional and institutional channels.

questions.question_text: A patient at a district hospital complains that staff members discuss the patient's condition loudly where other patients can hear. Which patient right is most directly affected?

choices.text: The right to privacy and confidentiality
The right to choose the hospital's financial administrator
The right to determine the duty roster
The right to access another patient's information

questions.rationale: Patients have a right to privacy and protection of confidential health information. Discussing identifiable clinical details where unauthorised persons can hear may violate this right.

questions.question_text: A patient receiving care at a regional hospital asks the nurse to explain the purpose of a proposed diagnostic procedure. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Tell the patient that asking questions is not permitted
Provide an appropriate explanation within the nurse's competence and facilitate further clarification from the responsible clinician when necessary
Ask the patient to sign a form without an explanation
Tell the patient that only relatives are entitled to information

questions.rationale: Patients have a right to understandable information about their care and proposed procedures. The nurse should answer within professional competence and refer questions requiring further clinical explanation to the responsible practitioner.

questions.question_text: A nurse is preparing a patient for a procedure, but the patient says that the explanation was not clear. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Proceed because the patient has already arrived at the hospital
Pause the preparation and ensure that the patient receives an adequate explanation before consent is obtained
Ask another patient to explain the procedure
Sign the consent form on the patient's behalf

questions.rationale: Consent is valid only when the patient has received and understood relevant information and has agreed voluntarily. The nurse should address the patient's questions and ensure that the appropriate consent process is followed before a non-emergency procedure.

questions.question_text: A competent adult patient refuses a blood transfusion for personal reasons after the risks and alternatives have been explained. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Force the transfusion because the nurse believes it is beneficial
Respect the refusal, communicate with the responsible clinical team and document the discussion
Ask relatives to sign consent against the patient's decision
Discharge the patient immediately without further assessment

questions.rationale: A competent adult generally has the right to refuse treatment after receiving relevant information. The nurse should ensure that the refusal is understood, communicate the decision to the clinical team and document the process appropriately.

questions.question_text: During a home visit, a nurse learns that a woman is living with HIV. A neighbour asks the nurse whether the woman has the infection. What should the nurse say?

choices.text: Confirm the diagnosis because the neighbour may be concerned
Explain that the nurse cannot disclose another person's private health information
Provide the diagnosis without mentioning the woman's name
Share the information if the neighbour promises to keep it secret

questions.rationale: A person's HIV status is confidential health information and should not be disclosed to neighbours without appropriate authority or justification. The nurse should protect the patient's privacy and avoid contributing to stigma or discrimination.

questions.question_text: A nurse needs to discuss a patient's clinical condition with another healthcare professional who is directly involved in the patient's care. Which action is appropriate?

choices.text: Share relevant information through an appropriate confidential channel
Discuss the case in a public market
Post the patient's full record in a community WhatsApp group
Share the information with anyone who asks about the patient

questions.rationale: Relevant information may be shared with authorised professionals for legitimate care purposes. The nurse should limit disclosure to what is necessary and use appropriate confidential communication channels.

questions.question_text: A nurse administers a medication and later realises that the wrong dose was given. What should the nurse do first?

choices.text: Alter the medication record to hide the error
Assess the patient promptly and initiate appropriate measures to reduce harm
Wait until the next shift to inform anyone
Blame the pharmacy without investigating the incident

questions.rationale: The immediate priority after a medication error is patient safety and assessment for potential harm. The nurse should promptly notify the appropriate clinician, follow incident-reporting procedures and document the facts accurately.

questions.question_text: A nurse discovers that a colleague has entered observations in a patient's record without actually assessing the patient. What is the most appropriate response?

choices.text: Ignore the entry because the patient appears comfortable
Raise the concern through appropriate supervisory channels and ensure the patient's condition is properly assessed
Copy the same observations into other patient records
Destroy the patient's record to prevent further errors

questions.rationale: Recording observations that were not performed compromises the accuracy and integrity of the patient record. The concern should be addressed through appropriate channels while ensuring that the patient receives a genuine assessment.

questions.question_text: A patient at a CHPS compound reports that a healthcare worker has repeatedly spoken to the patient in a humiliating manner. What should the community health nurse do?

choices.text: Dismiss the complaint because the worker is senior
Listen respectfully, protect the patient's dignity and guide the patient through the appropriate complaint process
Tell the patient to stop attending the facility
Publicly accuse the healthcare worker before establishing the facts

questions.rationale: Patient advocacy includes protecting dignity and supporting patients who raise concerns about their care. The nurse should listen objectively, explain available complaint channels and ensure that the concern is handled appropriately.

questions.question_text: A patient with a disability arrives at a district hospital and has difficulty accessing the consultation area. Which action best demonstrates patient advocacy?

choices.text: Tell the patient to return when another person is available
Help arrange reasonable access and appropriate assistance while respecting the patient's dignity
Ask the patient to abandon the consultation
Allow other patients to decide whether the patient should receive care

questions.rationale: Advocacy requires supporting equitable access to healthcare and protecting the dignity of people with disabilities. Reasonable assistance should be arranged without unnecessary discrimination or loss of patient autonomy.

questions.question_text: A community health nurse visits a household where a mother refuses immunisation for her eligible child because of misinformation. What is the most appropriate initial response?

choices.text: Threaten the mother with punishment
Listen to her concerns, provide accurate information and discuss the benefits and risks of immunisation
Vaccinate the child secretly
Record the child as immunised without administering the vaccine

questions.rationale: The nurse should use respectful communication and evidence-based health education to address the mother's concerns. Coercion, secret vaccination and falsification of records are inappropriate and undermine trust and ethical practice.

questions.question_text: A nurse conducting a home visit finds that an older adult is being neglected by family members. Which action is most appropriate?

choices.text: Ignore the situation because it occurs within a private household
Assess the person's immediate safety and care needs, document objective findings and follow appropriate referral and reporting procedures
Publicly shame the family in the community
Remove the person from the household without following any procedure

questions.rationale: The nurse has a responsibility to identify risks to vulnerable people and respond appropriately. Assessment, objective documentation and referral through established channels help protect the person while respecting legal and professional procedures.

questions.question_text: A patient offers a nurse an expensive personal gift in appreciation for the care received. What is the most appropriate response?

choices.text: Accept the gift secretly
Politely decline or manage the offer according to professional and facility policies
Demand a more expensive gift
Promise preferential treatment in exchange for the gift

questions.rationale: Accepting expensive gifts may create conflicts of interest or the appearance of exploitation and preferential treatment. Nurses should maintain professional boundaries and follow applicable institutional guidance on gifts.

questions.question_text: A nurse becomes close to a patient during repeated home visits and begins requesting personal loans from the patient's family. Which professional concern does this raise?

choices.text: Appropriate therapeutic communication
A breach of professional boundaries
Effective patient advocacy
Appropriate delegation of responsibilities

questions.rationale: Requesting personal loans from patients or their relatives can exploit the professional relationship and create inappropriate financial dependence. Nurses must maintain clear boundaries and avoid using their position for personal benefit.

questions.question_text: A nurse observes that expired medicines are being kept for use at a CHPS compound. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Use the medicines before they are noticed
Prevent their use, report the issue through appropriate channels and follow procedures for handling expired stock
Mix the expired medicines with unexpired stock
Sell the medicines to community members at a reduced price

questions.rationale: Expired medicines should not be administered because their quality, safety or effectiveness may no longer be assured. The nurse should protect patients and report the stock issue for appropriate disposal or management.

questions.question_text: A nurse is documenting care provided during a home visit. Which entry is most appropriate?

choices.text: Patient was difficult and refused to cooperate
Patient reported dizziness on standing; blood pressure was assessed and findings communicated to the supervising clinician
Patient is probably exaggerating symptoms
Everything was fine during the visit

questions.rationale: The second entry records the patient's reported symptom, an assessment and the action taken in objective language. Professional documentation should avoid judgemental comments and vague statements.

questions.question_text: A nurse is assigned to a community where the nurse's personal beliefs differ from those of some residents. How should the nurse approach care?

choices.text: Refuse care to residents whose beliefs are different
Provide respectful, non-discriminatory care while maintaining professional standards
Attempt to force residents to adopt the nurse's beliefs
Provide care only to people who share the nurse's beliefs

questions.rationale: Professional nursing practice requires respect for patients' dignity, beliefs and cultural backgrounds. Personal differences should not result in discrimination or denial of appropriate care.

questions.question_text: A patient who is about to undergo a procedure appears confused and cannot explain the information provided. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Assume consent because the patient is physically present
Raise concerns about the patient's understanding and ensure decision-making capacity and the consent process are appropriately assessed
Ask another patient to sign the consent form
Proceed because the procedure has already been scheduled

questions.rationale: Valid consent requires that the person has the capacity to make the particular decision and understands the relevant information. The nurse should alert the responsible clinician when there are concerns about understanding or decision-making capacity.

questions.question_text: During a home visit, a nurse needs to assess a patient's private health concern. Which action best protects the patient's privacy?

choices.text: Discuss the concern in front of all neighbours
Ask to speak with the patient in a private and appropriate setting
Share the information with the community leader without justification
Discuss the patient's condition loudly at the household entrance

questions.rationale: Privacy involves protecting patients from unnecessary exposure during discussions, examinations and care. The nurse should make reasonable arrangements for a confidential conversation, taking account of the patient's preferences and safety.

questions.question_text: A patient complains that the patient cannot understand the language used during a clinical explanation. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Continue explaining in the same language
Arrange appropriate language assistance so the patient can understand the information
Ask the patient to sign the consent form without further explanation
Tell the patient that language difficulties remove the right to information

questions.rationale: Patients should receive information in a form they can understand so they can participate meaningfully in care decisions. Appropriate language assistance supports communication, autonomy and informed consent.

questions.question_text: A nurse gives the same respectful attention to patients with NHIS coverage and patients paying privately. Which ethical principle is demonstrated?

choices.text: Justice
Fidelity
Veracity
Autonomy

questions.rationale: Justice requires fair and non-discriminatory treatment of patients. A person's insurance or payment arrangement should not be used as a reason to provide disrespectful or clinically inappropriate care.

questions.question_text: A community health nurse is conducting a routine home visit when a caregiver reports that a child has suddenly developed severe difficulty breathing and bluish lips. What should the nurse do first?

choices.text: Complete the household assessment form
Initiate an immediate emergency assessment and arrange urgent referral
Advise the caregiver to bring the child to the next child welfare clinic
Continue with the planned health education session

questions.rationale: Severe breathing difficulty and bluish lips suggest potentially life-threatening respiratory compromise. Immediate emergency assessment, appropriate initial care and urgent referral take priority over routine home-visit activities.

questions.question_text: At a CHPS compound, a patient develops heavy bleeding from a wound while another patient requests a routine dressing change. What is the priority action?

choices.text: Complete the routine dressing change first
Attend immediately to the patient with heavy bleeding and initiate appropriate bleeding control
Ask both patients to return the following day
Complete the daily attendance register

questions.rationale: Heavy bleeding can rapidly lead to circulatory compromise and requires immediate intervention. Routine wound care should be delayed until the urgent threat has been addressed.

questions.question_text: A nurse realises that an entry in a patient's record contains an incorrect date. What is the appropriate action?

choices.text: Erase the entry completely
Correct the error according to documentation policy while preserving the original entry and audit trail
Remove the entire page from the patient's file
Leave the error uncorrected because the clinical information is accurate

questions.rationale: Corrections should preserve the integrity and traceability of the original record. The nurse should follow the approved correction procedure, ensuring that the accurate information is clearly identifiable and authenticated.

questions.question_text: A community health nurse discovers that a patient cannot afford transport to a district hospital for a recommended referral. What is the most appropriate response?

choices.text: Cancel the referral because the patient cannot pay for transport
Explore available referral support and communicate with appropriate services while explaining the importance of timely care
Tell the patient to borrow money from any available person without further assistance
Record that the patient refused referral without discussing the barrier

questions.rationale: The nurse should recognise financial and transport barriers that may prevent access to necessary healthcare. Advocacy includes helping the patient explore available support and coordinating appropriate referral arrangements.

questions.question_text: A patient sends a nurse repeated personal messages late at night that are unrelated to healthcare. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Encourage a personal relationship with the patient
Maintain professional boundaries and redirect communication to appropriate healthcare channels
Share personal and intimate information to build trust
Promise special treatment in exchange for continued communication

questions.rationale: Professional boundaries help keep the nurse-patient relationship focused on healthcare needs. The nurse should communicate respectfully while maintaining appropriate limits and using approved channels for clinical contact.

questions.question_text: A nurse observes that a colleague has been collecting unofficial payments from patients for services that should be provided through the facility's approved payment process. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Participate so that the nurse can receive a share
Document relevant facts and report the suspected misconduct through appropriate institutional channels
Ignore the matter because the colleague is senior
Publicly publish the patients' names and payment details

questions.rationale: Unofficial collection of patient payments may constitute misconduct and can undermine trust and equitable access to care. The nurse should report the concern responsibly, provide factual information and protect patient confidentiality.

questions.question_text: A nurse provides pain relief to a patient after assessing the patient's condition and checking the prescribed treatment. Which ethical principle is most directly demonstrated?

choices.text: Beneficence
Veracity
Justice
Fidelity

questions.rationale: Beneficence requires nurses to take actions that promote patient welfare and relieve suffering. Providing appropriate pain management after assessment is an example of promoting the patient's well-being.

questions.question_text: A patient at a regional hospital asks to know the name and professional role of the person providing nursing care. What is the most appropriate response?

choices.text: Refuse because patients are not allowed to know who is caring for them
Identify oneself and explain one's professional role appropriately
Give another nurse's name to avoid questions
Tell the patient that professional identification is a private matter

questions.rationale: Patients are entitled to respectful communication and relevant information about the healthcare professionals involved in their care. Identifying oneself promotes transparency, trust and professional accountability.

questions.question_text: A community health nurse is preparing to leave for scheduled home visits when the CHPS compound receives a report of a pregnant woman experiencing convulsions. What should the nurse do first?

choices.text: Continue with the scheduled home visits
Prioritise emergency response, arrange immediate assessment and urgent referral
Wait for the next routine antenatal clinic
Ask the family to monitor the woman without contacting a health facility

questions.rationale: Convulsions during pregnancy may indicate eclampsia, a life-threatening obstetric emergency. Immediate emergency response and urgent referral are required, and routine activities must be postponed.

questions.question_text: A nurse is asked to sign a patient's record confirming that a wound dressing was performed, although the nurse did not perform or observe the procedure. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Sign because the colleague is trusted
Refuse to authenticate an event that cannot be verified and follow the appropriate reporting procedure
Sign and add a different date
Ask another staff member to sign in the nurse's place

questions.rationale: Signing an entry without a proper basis may create a false or misleading patient record. Nurses should authenticate only documentation for which they can take professional responsibility and should raise concerns through appropriate channels.

questions.question_text: A nurse learns during a home visit that a competent adult patient does not want the patient's diagnosis disclosed to relatives. The relatives later ask the nurse for details. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Disclose the diagnosis because relatives are entitled to all health information
Respect the patient's confidentiality and explain that information cannot be disclosed without appropriate authorisation or legal justification
Tell the relatives the diagnosis but ask them not to share it
Give the relatives access to the patient's complete record

questions.rationale: A competent adult patient's confidentiality should be respected, including in relation to family members. Disclosure requires appropriate consent, legal authority or another recognised justification.

questions.question_text: A nurse explains a proposed procedure to a patient, but the patient appears frightened and agrees only after the nurse threatens to withhold all future care. Which conclusion is most appropriate?

choices.text: The consent is valid because the patient verbally agreed
The consent may not be valid because the patient's decision was influenced by coercion
The consent is valid because the nurse is authorised to make the decision
The consent is valid if another nurse witnesses the signature

questions.rationale: Valid informed consent must be voluntary and free from coercion or undue pressure. The nurse should stop the process, address the patient's concerns and ensure that the decision is made freely after adequate information is provided.

questions.question_text: A CHPS compound has one available bed and two patients require admission for observation. One patient has signs of shock, while the other is clinically stable. Which decision best reflects ethical and clinical prioritisation?

choices.text: Admit the patient who arrived first regardless of clinical condition
Prioritise the patient with signs of shock for immediate emergency management and arrange appropriate care for the stable patient
Admit the patient who can pay more
Allow the patients' relatives to decide who receives care

questions.rationale: The patient with signs of shock has an immediate threat to life and requires urgent intervention. Ethical resource allocation should consider clinical urgency and fairness rather than payment ability or social influence.

questions.question_text: A patient develops a pressure injury after prolonged immobility in a hospital. The record shows that risk assessments and repositioning were not documented. Which statement is the most appropriate legal and professional interpretation?

choices.text: The absence of documentation automatically proves that negligence occurred
The missing documentation raises concerns about whether appropriate preventive care was assessed, planned and provided
The pressure injury cannot be related to nursing care
The nurse is legally responsible for every pressure injury regardless of circumstances

questions.rationale: Missing documentation may make it difficult to establish what assessments and preventive interventions were performed. However, negligence must be determined from the full facts, including the duty of care, standard of care, breach and resulting harm.

questions.question_text: A community health nurse stores identifiable patient information on a personal phone that has no password or other security protection. The phone is later lost. Which professional concern is most significant?

choices.text: The nurse has improved access to patient information
The loss may expose confidential patient information to unauthorised access
The loss automatically transfers ownership of the records to the finder
The incident has no significance if the nurse remembers the patients' names

questions.rationale: Unprotected storage of identifiable health information creates a risk of unauthorised disclosure when a device is lost. The nurse should report the incident promptly and follow applicable facility procedures for responding to information security breaches.

questions.question_text: A patient with limited financial resources is repeatedly asked to delay an urgent assessment while patients who can pay privately are attended to first, despite having less urgent conditions. Which ethical concern is most evident?

choices.text: Appropriate application of patient autonomy
Potential discrimination and violation of the principle of justice
Appropriate professional boundary management
A normal application of fidelity

questions.rationale: Prioritising patients according to ability to pay rather than clinical need raises concerns about inequity and discrimination. The nurse should advocate for fair access and raise the concern through appropriate channels.

questions.question_text: During a home visit, a nurse discovers that a child may be experiencing physical abuse. The caregiver asks the nurse not to tell anyone because the matter is a family issue. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Promise absolute secrecy and leave without assessing the child
Prioritise the child's safety, document objective findings and follow applicable child protection reporting and referral procedures
Confront the suspected perpetrator publicly without considering the child's safety
Ignore the concern unless the child makes a formal written complaint

questions.rationale: A suspected child protection concern must be handled with the child's safety and best interests as central considerations. The nurse should avoid promising absolute secrecy and should use established reporting and referral pathways rather than conducting an unauthorised investigation.

questions.question_text: A nurse reports a colleague's suspected unsafe practice to the supervisor using factual information. The colleague later accuses the nurse of disloyalty. Which professional judgement is most appropriate?

choices.text: The nurse acted improperly because loyalty requires silence
The nurse demonstrated professional accountability by raising a patient safety concern through an appropriate channel
The nurse should withdraw the report to maintain friendship
The nurse should publish the allegation on social media

questions.rationale: Professional accountability requires nurses to act when they identify credible risks to patient safety. Concerns should be raised honestly, objectively and through appropriate channels rather than concealed or publicised irresponsibly.

questions.question_text: A nurse provides repeated home visits to a patient and begins using the patient's personal information to obtain money from the patient's relatives. Which conclusion is most appropriate?

choices.text: The nurse is demonstrating effective community mobilisation
The nurse is exploiting the professional relationship and breaching professional boundaries
The nurse is applying the principle of beneficence
The nurse is appropriately advocating for the patient

questions.rationale: Using a patient's private information for personal financial gain is an abuse of professional trust. It violates confidentiality and professional boundaries and may constitute serious professional misconduct.

questions.question_text: At a district hospital, a nurse receives reports about four patients: one has sudden facial weakness and slurred speech, another requests routine medication advice, a third needs a dressing review, and a fourth is waiting for a health education session. Which patient requires the most immediate attention?

choices.text: The patient with sudden facial weakness and slurred speech
The patient requesting routine medication advice
The patient waiting for a dressing review
The patient waiting for health education

questions.rationale: Sudden facial weakness and slurred speech may indicate an acute stroke and require urgent assessment and escalation. Prompt intervention is important because delays may affect treatment options and patient outcomes.

questions.question_text: A nurse knows that a patient requires urgent referral, but the patient's family requests that the patient remain at home because they fear community criticism. The patient is competent and agrees to referral. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Follow the family's preference because relatives always make healthcare decisions
Support the patient's informed decision, explain the urgency and facilitate appropriate referral
Cancel the referral to avoid conflict with the family
Disclose the patient's condition to community members to pressure the family

questions.rationale: A competent adult patient's informed decision should guide the care decision rather than an overriding family preference. The nurse should respect autonomy, address concerns sensitively and facilitate safe access to the recommended care.

questions.question_text: A nurse administers a medication without checking the patient's allergy history. The patient develops a serious allergic reaction. Which elements are most relevant when assessing possible negligence?

choices.text: The nurse's age, length of service and personal beliefs
The duty of care, expected standard of practice, possible breach, causation and resulting harm
The patient's occupation and social status
The number of patients waiting at the facility alone

questions.rationale: A negligence assessment considers whether a duty existed, whether the required standard was breached, and whether the breach caused legally recognised harm. Failure to check relevant allergy information may be significant, but the full circumstances must be examined.

questions.question_text: A patient at a regional hospital asks for an explanation of the estimated cost of a proposed service and how the NHIS may apply. The nurse dismisses the request and tells the patient to pay without further discussion. Which response would better uphold the patient's rights?

choices.text: Refuse to discuss any aspect of the patient's financial concern
Direct the patient to the appropriate billing or NHIS personnel and facilitate clear information about applicable charges and coverage
Promise that NHIS will cover every possible service
Tell the patient to borrow money before asking further questions

questions.rationale: Patients should receive appropriate information about services and relevant financial arrangements. The nurse should avoid making unsupported promises about NHIS coverage and should help the patient obtain accurate information from the responsible personnel.

questions.question_text: A community health nurse is caring for a competent adult with a serious infectious disease. The patient refuses to inform a close contact who may be at risk. Which response is most appropriate?

choices.text: Immediately disclose all patient information to the community
Encourage the patient to take appropriate steps to protect the contact, seek guidance through authorised public health procedures and disclose only where legally justified
Ignore the possible risk to the contact under all circumstances
Post the patient's diagnosis on a public noticeboard

questions.rationale: This situation requires balancing confidentiality with the duty to prevent serious harm and comply with applicable public health requirements. The nurse should seek appropriate professional guidance and avoid unnecessary disclosure beyond what is legally and ethically justified.
